attributes.review:
I wouldn’t be writing this review, if I had been capable of talking to actual person! In the middle of the night, while I was asleep, someone succeeded at hacking into one of my Instagram accounts…after only two failed attempts! At the time of the first two attempts, which, again, happened while I was asleep, Instagram sent codes to my phone. On the third attempt, a message was sent to me via WhatsApp, informing me that my account had been accessed. That was just after 2AM. 

When I discovered these messages, after I woke up, at around 8AM, I clicked on a link that required me to verify whether it was me who had logged in. I, of course, clicked on “This wasn’t me.” Nothing happened! Every time I tried clicking on that option, a message popped up saying, “Something went wrong. Please try again.” It just said that over and over again. I was horrified. I had two Instagram accounts. The one that was hacked into, I simply deleted because I wasn’t using it that much anyway. 

The big problem is, the account that was hacked into was connected to my other, more important account, as well as my Facebook profile. I wonder what information the hacker stole! Lord knows, they had plenty of time to take whatever they wanted! The most I could do was chat with an AI bot about it! I gave this app two stars, instead of one, only because there is plenty about Instagram that I actually like, but what is it worth to have such a social media account when things like this can happen so easily?!
attributes.title: Questionable security and no human being to talk to about it!

attributes.review: Dear Instagram Developers, I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to offer a few suggestions that I believe would greatly benefit and enhance the functionality of Instagram. Firstly, I propose the inclusion of a feature that would allow users to add music to their profiles. This addition would undoubtedly add a whole new dimension of creativity and personalization, empowering users to express themselves through their favorite tunes. Secondly, I would like to address a concern regarding the white circle that surrounds the profile photo. In my opinion, this visual element can sometimes disrupt the overall aesthetic and proportion of the photo. I respectfully suggest that the option to remove or customize this circle be made available, allowing users to further curate their profiles in alignment with their personal branding. Last but not least, I would like to express my desire for Instagram to support the option of using GIFs as profile photos. This animated form of self-expression would undoubtedly inject a playful and engaging element into users' profiles, increasing their appeal and individuality. I genuinely believe that these proposals could positively impact the Instagram user experience, fostering increased creativity and allowing for further personalization. I appreciate your time and consideration, and I eagerly look forward to seeing the continued evolution of the platform. Thank you for your attention to these suggestions.
attributes.title: Creative and User-Enhancing Suggestions

Why can't I have larger photos? Why no zooming? The filters are useless. As a photographer I like the concept, but not the implementation. Update: I still use it. The sharing capability is too useful to pass up. But, being able to share higher resolution photos would be way more useful than sharing video. Update 2: the only way I tweet photos. All previous comments stand. It's just a better method for posting photos than native Twitter. Update 3: Still an awesome service with a few weird limitations. Why no native iPad app? Update 4: the filters are less useless now, except I still don't use them. I don't know if it's sized better on an iPad, but it must be. Works fine on an iPhone 6+. Once again, the handling of videos works well, but I would prefer higher res images to video. Update 5 for the latest version: all comments as before. I would prefer resizable photos to video and any filters. Art is firstly in the capture of the photographic moment. Secondly in the cropping. Lastly in any treatment or processing or modification. Update 6: so "larger" photos are allowed now, but still no zooming in the client. Not enough new features to up my rating. Did the iPad compatible app ever happen? Update 7: large photos. Client zooming. Bam! 5 stars. Update 8: too many advertisements. 3 stars.
Update 9: 2stars. Dark Mode! What Crap. Young developers are blinded by a lack of experience. Good developers gave up on this 40 years ago when we finally got systems that could do white backgrounds.
attributes.title: Pics too small. Dark background is horrible.

attributes.review: Whats up developers, 13 year IG veteran here. Hope all is well. I have two questions for you. (1.) Would you enforce us to make pancakes without flour if you discovered gluten-free methods were becoming popular? (2.) Would you eradicate the usage of all pens or pencils just because we now have the keyboard? No. I’m sure you wouldn’t. As a matter of fact, I believe you would provide us with the option to decide. The rectangular grid system is uprooting a fundamental element that made IG what it was. Remember back in the day when IG filters came with a SQUARE frame option? In the grand scheme of things, this is obviously a 1st world problem, but in regards to making the decision to keep the rectangular system, I’ve noticed that even you haven’t made your mind up. You’ve changed it back and forth several times, and of my two profiles, sometimes one of them has a square profile grid, and the other has rectangle, and that’s just from me toggling from one to the other in the same minute. I believe a rectangle display works as a fantastic method for displaying IG Reels, but I think we can all agree that squares are a foundational display method. I would suggest maybe adding an option in the settings menu so users, like myself, have the option to display a rectangular or square profile feed at their own discretion. Hope this helps.
attributes.title: Square Grids are an IG Staple

attributes.review:
I love Instagram, it’s my go-to social media and it’s the one I’m most comfortable using. However, this morning after updating, certain posts refuse to load, and most of them are the most recent posts on some of my favorite accounts. Videos are struggling to load and buffer way more than usual. I’ve tried closing the app and reopening it, going to the post on the account and trying to refresh it, whatever you can think of, and it’s not working.
Also I am not a fan of the new profile layout. I have a couple different accounts and each of them seems to have one of three different layouts and it really bothers me. 
I preferred when it was normal, and you had your post/follower/following count across the top, then the edit profile below that, your account description, stories, and then the post overview/scrolling/tagged photos option across the bottom.
Now on some of my accounts, you have to tap on a post in the overview in order to scroll through your posts, and you can’t see just one post at a time. I don’t like it. If I wanted to scroll through them I would have used the scrolling option. When I tap on a photo in the overview I want to just see that post. There also seems to be a waste of blank space on the profile, which is for stories I’m sure, but I’m not posting stories so it should just collapse down and not waste space on my profile.
I do still love the app, and it’s not like I’m going to stop using it now after all these years, but these are just some new things that have come up and I’m not a fan at all.
attributes.title: Newest update?
